description: Rhythm rules JSON Schema cannot express. Each rule has a severity; error blocks, warn is a notice. Every rule id is implemented in schema/semantic_validate.py (RULES) and verify_all.py fails if the two sets drift.

rules.description: shell.page-layers is first, shell.navbar second, shell.mobile-menu third; shell.preloader (when present) fourth and shell.bg-pixels-overlay immediately after it.
At most one HERO-category section per page; every template has exactly one except the named hero-less templates, which open with a content header (content.post-header / content.case-header) instead.

exceptions.reason: Detail pages open with a header block, not a hero (src/pages/BlogPostPage.jsx, CaseStudyPage.jsx)

rules.description: shell.footer-bottom-reveal is the last node, except that shell.call-alex-modal may follow it; shell.footer (when present) immediately precedes it.

exceptions.reason: ia/ia.json lists the modal after the footer on home and /compare

rules.description: shell.call-alex-modal requires a section that exposes a Call Alex link: hero.home or conversion.cta (the /compare hero has no Call Alex link).

conversion.cta contains a Call Alex link that opens the shell modal; without shell.call-alex-modal the link is inert. KNOWN GAP: the four CMS templates (blog index/post, case-studies index/study) are built without the modal although live renders it there (templates.json knownGaps LIVE_MODAL_ON_CMS_TEMPLATES).
transition.black-to-white and transition.white-to-black appear together or not at all, black-to-white first.
No two transition.* sections are adjacent (each pixel grid bridges real content).
Every section whose surface is "light" lies between transition.black-to-white and transition.white-to-black, and every section between that pair is "light" (the white-section surface).
content.read-next appears only with content.case-header (blog posts hide the equivalent block on live and it is not rendered).
conversion.cta does not accompany hero.book-a-demo or legal.content (observed absent on /book-a-demo and the 3 legal routes).
Adjacent sections should not share a category, for the categories where adjacency would mean redundancy.

exceptions.reason: Real pages place several sections of these categories back to back by design (home: 4 PROOF, 4 PRODUCT, 3 FIT; /compare: COMPARE run; detail pages: CONTENT run; SHELL stack); TRANSITION adjacency is its own error rule

keyingNote: No section legitimately repeats on a page in this site (the white variants of specialties/integrations are separate section ids: compare.specialty-white, compare.integrations-white), so structural rules key on section id. If a section ever repeats with different variants, key the rules on (section, variant).

categories.SHELL: Chrome present across many or all routes: navigation, mobile menu, background layers, preloader, popup, footer.
categories.HERO: Page-opening header block: a headline, and where the template has one, a primary call to action or form.
categories.PROOF: Homepage-only social proof: client logos, case-study spotlight, metrics, testimonials.
categories.PRODUCT: Homepage-only product explanation and its four agent modules.
categories.TRANSITION: Scroll-scrubbed pixel-grid transitions between dark and light surfaces, shared by templates that carry a dark/white split.
categories.FIT: Homepage-only buyer-fit content: specialties, EMR integrations, security/compliance.
categories.CONVERSION: Closing call-to-action block, reused across every marketing and content template.
categories.LEGAL: Legal template content (Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, HIPAA).
categories.CONTENT: Blog and case-study index and detail content, data-driven from content/*.json.
